context: Current closing price of Boston Scientific (BSX): $44.35 USD as of 2026-06-26.
justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift over time from what I assume was a baseline near 44.5. At the one-day horizon, the estimate stays very close to the current level because short-term price or index movements tend to mean-revert around recent values absent a specific catalyst, so I anchored tightly to the prevailing observation. Over one week, I nudged the estimate slightly higher to 44.8, reflecting a mild directional bias that could stem from recent momentum or a marginally positive macro backdrop. By one month, the drift to 45.5 incorporates the compounding of that same gentle trend, though the further out we go, the more that point estimate is essentially a best-guess center of a wide distribution rather than a confident prediction.

The confidence interval widths widen substantially as the horizon extends, and this reflects the fundamental reality that uncertainty compounds with time. At one day, the 90% interval spans roughly 1.3 units on each side, consistent with typical daily volatility being relatively contained. At one week, the interval nearly doubles in half-width to about 2.3 units, capturing the possibility of several days of adverse or favorable moves accumulating. By one month, the interval opens to a full 5 units on each side, reflecting that over thirty days, sentiment shifts, data releases, and liquidity conditions can move prices substantially in either direction.

Several known sources of risk could drive outcomes outside even these wider intervals. Sudden macroeconomic shocks — an unexpected inflation print, a central bank surprise, or a credit event — could gap the underlying well beyond the one-month bounds. Geopolitical escalation or a liquidity crunch could cause sharp, discontinuous moves that short-window historical volatility estimates simply do not capture well.

On the upside, an unexpectedly strong earnings season, a dovish policy pivot, or a resolution of an ongoing geopolitical tension could push values meaningfully above 50.5 within the month. These tail events are, by construction, outside the 90% interval, meaning I assign roughly a 10% combined probability to outcomes beyond those bounds — but it is worth emphasizing that financial distributions tend to have fat tails, so the true probability of extreme outcomes is likely modestly higher than a normal-distribution framework would suggest.
